name: Splunk
description: Search Splunk logs and metrics from Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot through Splunk's official MCP Server: run SPL and saved searches, list indexes, hosts and sources, read knowledge objects, and draft SPL with Splunk AI Assistant.
instructions:
This connector bridges the **Splunk MCP Server**, the official app by Splunk (Splunkbase app 7931), on your Splunk Cloud Platform or Splunk Enterprise search head. Splunk's own server provides the tools: SPL searches, saved searches, indexes, hosts and sources, knowledge objects, KV Store, users and, where Splunk AI Assistant is available, the `saia_*` tools that write, explain and optimise SPL. AnythingMCP puts them behind your MCP endpoint with OAuth for Claude and ChatGPT, per-tool roles, the audit log and response mapping, next to your other systems.

**The tools come from your server.** At install AnythingMCP asks your Splunk MCP Server which tools it has, so you get exactly the set of the app version you run. After upgrading the app in Splunk, open the connector and click **Discover tools** to pick up new ones.

**Setup (about 10 minutes, needs a Splunk admin)**:
1. Install **Splunk MCP Server** from Splunkbase on the search head (or search head cluster). Make sure REST API access and token authentication are enabled.
2. Give the role that will run the tools the `mcp_tool_execute` capability, and restrict that role to the indexes the AI may read. The role is the real boundary: the agent sees whatever this user sees.
3. In the Splunk MCP Server app, generate an **encrypted MCP token** for that user and copy it (Splunk shows it once). An ordinary Splunk user or service token does not work: Splunk refuses it with "invalid token audience" (HTTP 403).
4. Fill in the variables and install:
   - `SPLUNK_HOST`: the search head's host name, without `https://` and without a port, for example `yourstack.splunkcloud.com`. The connector calls `https://SPLUNK_HOST:8089/services/mcp`, the address the app shows. If yours uses another port or path, change the base URL in the connector editor after installing.
   - `SPLUNK_MCP_TOKEN`: the encrypted token from step 3. It is stored encrypted.

**Network**: AnythingMCP connects to the management port (8089). On Splunk Cloud Platform that port only answers addresses on your stack's IP allow list for the search API (Admin Config Service), so add the address AnythingMCP calls from (on AnythingMCP Cloud, ask support for the current egress IP). Splunk Enterprise needs a certificate on 8089 that the AnythingMCP server trusts.

**Safety**: Splunk marks `splunk_run_query` and `splunk_run_saved_search` as able to change data, because SPL can write (`collect`, `outputlookup`, `delete`). Give the token's user a role that cannot write to indexes or lookups. The two dashboard tools install switched off; turn them on per tool if the AI should create or change dashboards. Splunk admins can also disable tools for everyone in the app, and **Invalidate all MCP access tokens** there revokes every token at once.

**Working with it**: start with `splunk_get_indexes` or `splunk_get_metadata` to see what data exists, always give searches a time range (`earliest`/`latest`) and a row limit, and let `saia_generate_spl` draft SPL you are unsure about. A 403 on install means the token is not an MCP token or the role lacks `mcp_tool_execute`; a timeout usually means the allow list or a firewall blocks port 8089.

tools.name: saia_ask_splunk_question
tools.description: Ask natural language questions about Splunk using Splunk AI Assistant. Get explanations about Splunk commands, concepts, features, and best practices.

prompt.description:
Natural language question about Splunk
Validation: Prompt is required and must be between 1 and 10000 characters (submitted: {length})

chat_history.description:
Chat history for context
Validation: Chat history is required and limited to 5000 characters

additional_context.description: Additional context to include in generated SPL

tools.name: splunk_create_dashboard
tools.description: Creates a new Splunk dashboard using Dashboard Studio JSON in the specified app namespace.

app.description: App namespace to create the dashboard in

eai_data.description: The full Dashboard Studio JSON definition

tools.name: splunk_get_index_info
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific Splunk index. Returns comprehensive configuration and status information for the specified index.

index_name.description:
Name of the index to get information about
Validation: Index name can only contain alphanumeric characters, underscores (_), and hyphens (-)

tools.name: splunk_get_indexes
tools.description: Get a list of indexes from Splunk. Indexes are data repositories where machine data is stored and organized.

count.description: Maximum number of results to return in this page. Omit this argument to use the server's configured default row limit. If you provide a value greater than the server's configured maximum row limit, the server uses the maximum instead.

offset.description: Zero-based index of the first result to return. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: splunk_get_info
tools.description: Get comprehensive information about the Splunk instance. Retrieves system information including version, hardware specs, and operational status.

tools.name: splunk_get_knowledge_objects
tools.description: Retrieve Splunk knowledge objects by type. Supports various knowledge object types including saved searches, alerts, field extractions, lookups, macros, data models, and more.

type.description: Type of knowledge object to retrieve

row_limit.description: Maximum number of rows to return

tools.name: splunk_get_kv_store_collections
tools.description: Get KV Store collection statistics including size, count, and storage information. Retrieves comprehensive metrics about all KV Store collections in the Splunk instance.

row_limit.description: Maximum number of rows to return

tools.name: splunk_get_metadata
tools.description: Retrieve metadata about hosts or sources across one or more indexes in the selected time window.

type.description: Metadata category to list (hosts or sources).

index.description:
Index name or wildcard pattern (e.g. main, app_*, *).
Validation: Index pattern may contain letters, numbers, underscore, dash, and * wildcard

row_limit.description: Maximum number of rows to return

tools.name: splunk_get_user_info
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information about the currently authenticated user including roles and permissions. Returns comprehensive user profile data for the current session.

tools.name: splunk_get_user_list
tools.description: Get a list of users from Splunk. Retrieves information about all users including authentication details, roles, and account status.

row_limit.description: Maximum number of rows to return

tools.name: splunk_run_query
tools.description: Execute a Splunk search query and return the results. Use this to retrieve log data, perform aggregations, analyze events, and extract insights. Always set the 'app' parameter when the user specifies an app context — omitting it means app-scoped field extractions will not be applied.

app.description:
Splunk app context to run the SPL query in (e.g., 'search', 'enterprise_security'). Set this when the user specifies an app — omitting it means app-scoped field extractions and lookups will not be applied.
Validation: App name may only contain letters, numbers, underscores, hyphens, and dots.

query.description:
Valid SPL query to execute
Validation: SPL query must be between 1 and 10000 characters (submitted: {length})

row_limit.description: Maximum number of rows to return

workload_pool.description:
Splunk workload pool to run this search in.
Validation: Workload pool name may only contain letters, numbers, underscores, hyphens, and dots.

tools.name: splunk_run_saved_search
tools.description: Execute a Splunk saved search by name and return its results. Saved searches are pre-defined SPL queries stored in Splunk. Use get_knowledge_objects with type='saved_searches' to discover available saved searches and their app context. If the saved search name is unique across apps, the app is resolved automatically. If the same name exists in multiple apps, the alphabetically first app is used; pass the 'app' parameter to target a specific app. If the saved search contains placeholder tokens like $token_name$, pass replacement values as key=value pairs in the args parameter.

app.description:
Splunk app context to run the saved search in (e.g., 'search', 'enterprise_security'). If omitted, the app is auto-resolved; when the name exists in multiple apps the alphabetically first app is used.
Validation: App name may only contain letters, numbers, underscores, hyphens, and dots.

args.description:
Optional replacement arguments for saved search tokens
Validation: args must be space-separated key="value" token assignments only (e.g. host="web01" sourcetype="syslog"). Pipe operators, brackets, backticks, semicolons, and newlines are not allowed in values.

row_limit.description: Maximum number of rows to return

latest_time.description: Override the saved search's default end time (e.g., now, -1h). If omitted, uses the time range configured in the saved search.

earliest_time.description: Override the saved search's default start time (e.g., -24h, -7d, 2024-01-01T00:00:00). If omitted, uses the time range configured in the saved search.

saved_search_name.description:
Name of the saved search to execute
Validation: Saved search name is required, it cannot be blank and is limited to 500 characters.
